deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft for Riemann's Göttingen Inaugural-Dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The previous page holds the article plan Art. 5-17. This page has two parts.

(A) Draft prose for the early articles (cf. Arts. 1 and 5 of the printed dissertation).
(i) Determination of the surface. Let T be a surface spread over the z-plane. If the position of its boundary and the positions of its winding (branch) points are given, then T is either completely determined or restricted to finitely many configurations. The ambiguity arises because these data may refer to different superposed sheets, so they can be glued in different ways. In modern terms: a finite branched covering of a planar region is fixed by its branch locus and boundary only up to finitely many monodromy choices.
(ii) Function concept. A quantity w that takes a determinate value at every point O of T, and that varies continuously with O 'allgemein zu reden' (exceptions on isolated lines and points not excluded), may be regarded as a function of x, y. All later 'functions of x, y' are to be understood in this sense. This is the Dirichlet-style concept of function, made locally continuous almost everywhere.
(iii) A transition sentence: before studying such functions, some remarks on the connectivity ('Zusammenhang') of a surface are sent ahead. This is Art. 6 in the plan.

(B) Revised plan, Arts. 16-19.
Art. 16: proof of the minimum theorem assumed in Art. 15 'mittelst der Grenzmethode', i.e. Riemann's version of the Dirichlet principle.

Art. 17: statement of the existence theorem.
- Data:
  - Cut T by cross-cuts (Querschnitte) into a simply connected T*.
  - Let α+βi be a given function of x, y with Ω(α,β) = ∫∫_T [(α_x − β_y)^2 + (α_y + β_x)^2] dT finite. The integrand is left blank ('∫ dT') on the page; it is supplied from the previous page.
- Claim: α+βi can always, and in only one way, be turned into an analytic function of z = x+iy by adding a function λ+μi of x, y such that:
  1) λ = 0 on the boundary of T, and μ is prescribed at one point;
  2) λ is continuous on T and μ on T*, except at isolated points, and only so discontinuous that ∫∫(λ_x^2+λ_y^2) dT and ∫∫(μ_x^2+μ_y^2) dT stay finite;
  3) the derivatives of μ agree on the two banks of each cross-cut, so μ jumps there only by constants (periods).
- Method (my reconstruction, consistent with the printed dissertation):
  - Minimise Ω(α+λ, β) = ∫∫[(α_x+λ_x−β_y)^2 + (α_y+λ_y+β_x)^2] dT over admissible λ vanishing on the boundary.
  - The Euler-Lagrange equation is ∂_x(u_x − β_y) + ∂_y(u_y + β_x) = 0 with u = α+λ. The β-terms cancel (β_yx = β_xy), leaving Δu = 0.
  - Then the form (−u_y − β_x) dx + (u_x − β_y) dy is closed. On simply connected T* it has a primitive μ, with μ_x = −(u_y+β_x) and μ_y = u_x − β_y.
  - Hence u_x = (β+μ)_y and u_y = −(β+μ)_x. These are the Cauchy-Riemann equations for u + i(β+μ).
  - The gradient of μ is single-valued on T, so μ has constant jumps across the cuts, and ∫|∇μ|^2 = Ω_min is finite.
- Uniqueness (mine): take the difference of two solutions. Its real part is single-valued and harmonic on T and zero on the boundary, so it vanishes. Its imaginary part is therefore constant, and the constant is fixed by the value at one point.

Art. 18: scope ('Umfang') of the conditions needed to determine a function of z inside a given region. The marginal '26' is probably a page count.
Art. 19: left empty.
The roman numerals III, II, I in the right margin seem to regroup the articles.
Bottom note: 'In Art. 19 an explanation of Art. 15 is to be inserted, ... [it] disturbs the position of the ...'.
Upside-down lines: largely illegible; possibly title or heading drafts ('Inhaltsverzeichnis' / 'Dissertation' are guesses).
errors: No mathematical error. Art. 17 tacitly presupposes the Dirichlet principle (existence of the minimiser), which is unjustified by later (Weierstrass 1870) standards. Riemann's 'Grenzmethode' in Art. 16 does not repair this rigorously.
Implicit: for the finite-Dirichlet-integral class to be meaningful, α and β must be regular enough, e.g. Ω(α,β) finite. Riemann states only that condition, which is what is needed.
The claim that T is fixed by boundary and branch points up to finitely many shapes is correct for finitely-sheeted coverings (finitely many monodromy choices). It is stated without proof.

results.what: Riemann surface determined by boundary and branch points up to finitely many configurations
results.modern_name: classification of finite branched coverings by branch locus and monodromy

results.what: Function of x,y defined as continuously varying value except on isolated lines/points
results.modern_name: general (Dirichlet) function concept / piecewise continuous functions

results.what: Art. 17: any α+βi with finite Ω can be made analytic, uniquely, by adding λ+μi with λ=0 on boundary, μ normalised at a point and with constant periods across cross-cuts
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle / existence of harmonic function with prescribed boundary data and its multivalued conjugate (periods on multiply connected domains)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft and table of contents for Riemann's 1851 dissertation. All content (branch-point determination of the surface, the function concept, the Dirichlet-principle existence theorem with cross-cuts) appears in the published dissertation. Only minor draft details (ordering of articles, the plan to insert a commentary on Art. 15) are new.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u=Function('u')(x,y); b=Function('b')(x,y); F=(diff(u,x)-diff(b,y))**2+(diff(u,y)+diff(b,x))**2; from sympy.calculus.euler import euler_equations; eq=euler_equations(F,[u],[x,y])[0]; simplify(eq.lhs + 2*(diff(u,x,2)+diff(u,y,2)))==0
checkable.asserts: The Euler-Lagrange equation of Ω in u=α+λ is Δu=0; the β terms cancel.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u=Function('u')(x,y); b=Function('b')(x,y); P=-(diff(u,y)+diff(b,x)); Q=diff(u,x)-diff(b,y); simplify(diff(Q,x)-diff(P,y)-(diff(u,x,2)+diff(u,y,2)))==0
checkable.asserts: The form P dx + Q dy defining μ is closed exactly when u is harmonic.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u=x**2-y**2; b=x*y; mu=integrate(diff(u,x)-diff(b,y),y); mu=mu+integrate(simplify(-(diff(u,y)+diff(b,x))-diff(mu,x)),x); [simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(b+mu,y)), simplify(diff(u,y)+diff(b+mu,x))]==[0,0]
checkable.asserts: Example: with harmonic u, the constructed μ makes u+i(β+μ) satisfy the Cauchy-Riemann equations.

transcription_corrections: 'werden wir in der Folge statt den Begriff einer Function festlegen' likely reads 'stets den Begriff'.
'Den Art. 19. Erläuterung von Art. 15. einzufügen' reads better as 'In Art. 19 Erläuterung von Art. 15 einzufügen'.
In Art. 17 the integrand of '∫ dT' is left blank on the page; it is presumably ((∂α/∂x−∂β/∂y)^2+(∂α/∂y+∂β/∂x)^2) as on the previous page.
Roman numerals III, II, I stand in the right margin beside Arts. 17, 18 and 19 respectively. They appear to mark a regrouping, not separate text.
